paragraphs: Rav Zevid, in Abaye’s name: Berakhot 46b; he said to Abaye: Sotah 32b. Amemar in his name. Rav Zevid’s daughter-in-law rebelled; Amemar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi sat …. Rav Gamda told them, “Because Rav Zevid is a great man, do you flatter him?” Ketubbot 63,end of side b. Rabbi Zeira said in Rav Zevid’s name: Avodah Zarah 14a. The rabbis praised to Rabbi Zeira a son of Rav Zevid, brother of Rabbi Shimon ben Zevid, as a great man expert in blessings. Rabbi Zeira said, “When he comes to you, bring him to me.” So in newer Talmud editions, Berakhot 38,end of side a. Rabbi Chiyya Parva visited the exilarch’s house …. Rabbi Zevid told them, “Do not heed him.” They gave Rav Zevid a draught of vinegar and he died: Avodah Zarah 38b. Those of the exilarch’s house were unworthy; because he was stringent with them, they gave it to him. Rav Zevid teaches thus, Rav Chinena son of Rav Ika teaches thus; Rav Kahana said to him: Meilah 19. Rav Kahana said to him, or to Rav Pappi: Sotah 45a. Rav Kahana eulogized him at the end of chapter Asarah Yuchasin (I did not find it). See Rav Zevid of Nehardea; Yuchasin erred, thinking this was the unqualified Rav Zevid. He also erred in the locator: it is in Moed Katan, not Asarah Yuchasin. Rav Menashe bar Zevid (see his entry). Rav Mari and Rav Zevid disagree (see his entry). He reported Rav Nachman: Bava Metzia 17a. Rav Pappa objected to Rav Zevid: Gittin 89b. Sheerit Yosef counts him among Rav’s students. It seems to me this derives from Bava Kamma 84a, Rav Zevid said in Rav’s name. It is a scribal error and should read Rava’s name; that matter at 85a is likewise in Rava’s name, as are Bava Batra 99b; Shabbat 93a; Rosh Hashanah 6,end of side a; Sukkah 44a; Bava Kamma 5,end of side a, 21b, 118b. All these places have Rava’s name. (Requires examination: Rabbi Zeira was in Rav Assi’s time, yet Rabbi Zeira reports him. This is not puzzling, for Rav Zevid reports Rava, and Rabbi Zeira called Rava “master.”) [Glosses: Zevid. Yevamot 96a; Avodah Zarah 33,beginning of side b: Rav Zevid bar Oshaya; so in Yuchasin. Newer Talmud editions: L.T. It is a scribal error, for Bava Metzia 92b has Rav Zevid bidve Rabbi Oshaya, and likewise Avodah Zarah 6b, 56a: Rav Zevid recited bidve Rabbi Oshaya; Rashi: in Rabbi Oshaya’s baraita. In Bava Batra 95a, Rav Zevid deve Rav Oshaya should read bidve; newer editions: L.T. Asheri too has beRabbi Oshaya. Shevuot 47a: “Rav Zevid bar Oshaya likewise recited”; some say “Rav Zevid recited: Rav Oshaya said”; requires examination. In newer editions: A.R. [א״ר], “Rav Zevid said: Rabbi Oshaya said.”]
